correctness.rationale: The disproof is mathematically complete. For a Bertrand prime q with Q0<q<=2Q0, q is eventually below the short interval, so no prime in the interval is divisible by q and E_0=0. Character orthogonality gives sum_a S(a/q)=0 while S(0)=T, hence some nonzero a has |S(a/q)|>=T/(q-1). Because q is prime this a/q is reduced, and its distance from every reduced a'/q' with q'<=Q0 is at least 1/(qq')>1/(2Q0^2), which eventually exceeds the stipulated major-arc width. Huxley's short-interval PNT at exponent 5/6 gives T~2h, so h/(log N)^A dominates h N^{-delta} for every fixed delta>0. The committed verifier correctly checks the finite identities and crossover arithmetic; the asymptotic proof does not depend on those finite spot checks.
